title: GPU capacity failover orchestration and queue-pressure experiments
creator: Nadia R. Patel
description: Summary: During a spike on 2026-03-08 we observed GPU pool exhaustion in multiple hosted regions. The symptom set was prolonged queue buildup (requests waiting >10s), large numbers of admission rejections, and several downstream customer errors. Root cause analysis indicated a combination of (1) a regressed admission-controller scoring change that made low-priority jobs perpetually deferred, (2) a suboptimal autoscaler tuning for short bursts, and (3) degraded dequeue throughput in the batching service due to a recently introduced mutex around KV cache eviction. This ticket tracks a set of mitigations, experiments, and durable orchestration changes to reduce mean-time-to-recovery and avoid repeated capacity exhaustion.
decision_log: 2026-03-09: Roll forward ephemeral mitigation - increased autoscale aggressiveness for burst window from 30s->120s (on-call change) to reduce queue growth.
2026-03-10: Reverted admission scoring change that prioritized long-tail low-cost jobs; documented in PR #4632.
2026-03-11: Agreed on three parallel tracks: quick triage playbook, controlled experiments for admission heuristics, and orchestration changes for pool failover. Owner: Marco Leung.
action_items: A1: Ship emergency autoscale profile with burst priming (owner: Marco) — ETA 2026-03-16 — status: in progress
A2: Remove global KV eviction mutex and replace with per-shard eviction (owner: Elena M.) — ETA 2026-03-20 — status: planned
A3: Implement soft per-customer concurrency caps + priority decay to prevent noisy tenants from queueing everything (owner: Ravi K.) — ETA 2026-04-02 — status: backlog
A4: Create runbook additions for on-call: detect queue pressure, alpha remedy knobs, and safe rollback steps (owner: Nadia) — ETA 2026-03-14 — status: done
A5: Add automated canary traffic to test autoscale rebound in staging and a synthetic load generator for 1x/3x/10x spike profiles (owner: SRE team) — ETA 2026-03-18 — status: in progress
experiments: E1: Priority preemption window: allow high-priority (tiered) jobs to preempt queued low-priority ones when queue_growth_rate > 5 reqs/s for 20s. Test in us-west-2 staging.
E2: Adaptive pool priming: when queue length crosses threshold, proactively spin new nodes with a 60s fast ramp vs. baseline 180s. Measure tail latency and cost delta.
E3: Admission score rework: introduce short-term score decay so deferred requests increase priority over time to prevent starvation.
E4: Batch drain optimization: microbenchmark per-shard eviction to validate improved dequeue throughput under mixed sequence-length workloads.
rollforward_plan: If experiments show >50% reduction in P99 queue_age without >15% cost increase deploy to prod with canary by region. Use canary traffic at 5% with automated rollback on error spike. Incrementally widen canary over 24h.
rollback_plan: If rollout increases 5xx/429 by >3x from baseline or user-facing errors spike for >10m, revert autoscale profile and admission changes, and re-enable previous admission parameters. Notify customers and open incident channel.
